questions.material:
A. Packing for a day out and printing a class poster

Packing for a day out can be easier when you think through the actual journey rather than collect everything you might possibly want. A useful bag supports the plan without becoming a burden.

Begin with the essential requirements. Tickets, agreed supplies and any instructions from the organiser should come before extra entertainment. ____1____ This prevents a full bag from hiding the one item you truly need.

Check how long you will carry the bag. A comfortable load at home may feel different after a long walk. ____2____ The journey matters as much as the destination.

Put things where you can reach them when needed. A ticket buried beneath lunch creates unnecessary searching at the entrance. ____3____ Small decisions about order can save repeated unpacking.

Keep appropriate items separate. A wet coat and dry paper should not share the same unprotected space. ____4____ Follow any specific storage guidance for food or equipment.

Finally, review the bag once it is packed. ____5____ Removing an unnecessary item can be more useful than finding another pocket. The aim is to carry what the day requires while leaving enough attention and energy to enjoy it.
questions.hint: Use the complete material and the question together.

options.text: A. Make a short list of essentials before choosing optional extras.
B. Ask whether every object has a clear role in the plan.
C. Consider the distance and available help before adding more weight.
D. Suitable separation can protect one item from another.
E. Some bags are displayed in shop windows beside shoes.
F. Place the next item you will use in an accessible compartment.
G. Many travellers keep photographs after returning from a holiday.

questions.material:
B. Packing for a day out and printing a class poster

Our class designed a poster for a reading afternoon. The teacher ____1____ (bring) a sample print so we could compare the page on a screen with one on paper. The two did not look exactly alike.

Several ____2____ (design) used a dark background. It made the title dramatic as well ____3____ easy to notice, but some small words became difficult to read. We needed to check the details, not only admire the first impression.

I looked at ____4____ (I) draft from the back of the room. A pale line had almost disappeared. The teacher asked me ____5____ (change) its colour before making another sample.

There was room ____6____ a short date line beneath the title. We made sure the date and place were not separated by a decorative picture. Someone looking quickly should be able to find both.

The second version was ____7____ (clear) than the first. We checked the spelling ____8____ (careful), comparing the words with the approved event details. Each poster ____9____ (check) before it was put on a noticeboard.

The finished design still used colour and pictures, but its practical information no longer depended on a viewer coming very close. We had tested it in a place like the one where people would see it. That was ____10____ useful step between making an attractive page and making a message that worked for its readers.
